headline: The site's own Content-Security-Policy was refusing a script the site itself serves. Cloudflare injects its Web Analytics beacon into every delivered document; script-src admitted 'self' plus four hashes. Production had collected ZERO pageviews and thrown a CSP violation on every page load, while every launch-readiness judgement about the public surface was being made without a single production datapoint. No automated check had ever seen it, because the edge injects the beacon only for browser-shaped requests and the verifier fetched with Accept: application/json — it was auditing a document no visitor ever receives.

items.title: Four of fourteen ranked findings existed only in HTTP responses, because two of the three stages that produce this site leave no trace in git
items.evidence: What ships here is source -> build-pages rewrite -> edge policy. build-pages injects per-page canonical and og:url tags that appear nowhere in source; the Cloudflare zone injects an analytics beacon whose hostname appears nowhere in the repository. A source-only audit of this project is therefore structurally blind, and had been. The four findings only production could show: the blocked beacon; content-hashed assets served max-age=14400 rather than immutable; zero modulepreload on a 48-module import graph; and the community API answering status warming with sampleSize 0 behind a widget sitting above the fold on the front door. The inverse also held and was recorded as a rejected phantom rather than ranked: 'public pages have no canonical tags' is true in source and false in production.

items.title: The verifier was asking the wrong question, which is why it stayed green through the defect it existed to catch
items.evidence: Measured on this origin across two routes: a request with a browser User-Agent and Accept: text/html returns a document containing the beacon; the same URL with Accept: application/json,text/plain,*/* does not. verify-edge-policy-application.mjs used the second form, so every prior 'edge policy applied' attestation was true about a document nobody is served. It now fetches as a browser does and asserts the served policy admits every external origin the served document requests, and reports UNPROVED rather than APPLIED when no document is supplied. The two admitted hosts were read out of beacon.min.js itself — the script origin, and https://cloudflareinsights.com/cdn-cgi/rum which it POSTs to — rather than taken from documentation, so an admitted-but-mute beacon cannot read as healthy.

items.title: The public-truth gate proved every number on the site and could not see that a page had stopped tracking the product
items.evidence: check-public-truth has verified the engine-system count, the rival-club count, four retired claims and internal vocabulary since S70, and ran green throughout a period in which status.html's newest release note sat at 2026-08-03 while lastSession was 93 — 24 sessions unpublished, including the entire S90-S93 calibration and owner-economy arc. A visitor reading Status concluded the game had been idle for three weeks. The gate now counts sessions between the newest published note and PROJECT_STATUS.lastSession, resolved through CURRENT_STATE so it tracks a moving target rather than a literal; tolerance is one session because the note lands at closeout. Negative control before the fix named the 24-session gap exactly. Five player-facing notes now cover S70-S93 and a sixth covers S94.

items.title: The Settings tab was the structural reason two god-mode surfaces survived thirty sessions
items.evidence: Twenty panel headings in one undifferentiated stack, spanning three audiences: consumer identity (Trophy Case, Brand Builder, Speedrun), live simulation economy (Owner Controls, Facilities Market, Coaching Staff), and developer diagnostics (Launch Readiness, System Health, a Realism Verification runner accepting up to 30 synchronous seasons, League Progression Parity, Finite-Number Integrity, Offseason Pipeline). The causal claim is evidenced, not asserted: S63 closed the Coaching Staff panel's three free number boxes and S93 closed the byte-identical Owner Facilities panel eight lines away in the same file, thirty sessions later. Both lived here. A tab that mixes trophies with live economy inputs and debug tables is a tab nobody design-reviews as gameplay. The economy now has a Boardroom surface that hydrates its own domains, and the seven diagnostics require ?dev=1 — a URL parameter rather than a stored preference, because a diagnostics surface a player can enable permanently by accident is the same defect one step removed.

items.title: Three ranked premises were corrected during implementation rather than implemented as written
items.evidence: The funnel item proposed landing content at / and setup at /play, which would have reversed DECISIONS 2026-08-04 ('The root URL is for the person who has never seen the game'). The real gap was narrower — S70 answered 'let a newcomer start' and never answered 'let a newcomer know why' — so the argument moved onto the root page BELOW the one-click start, and a Playwright spec asserts the ordering rather than the presence. The rival-persona item claimed personas were invisible; rivalTradeOffers.js:212-213 already attached gmName and gmLine, and beatReporter names the winning GM on a free-agency outbid, so half the item did not exist and only the faceless on-clock draft market and the Load-Archetypes button shipped. The visual-QA item rested on 'the receipts already carry the hashes', which was true of 84 captures out of 821 — all from one session. A fourth item, the 14-to-6 tab regroup, was skipped entirely: the rail is already grouped under five task headers, so migrating fourteen panels against a 1,220-test suite would have been churn for no measured benefit.

items.title: A code review found ten defects in this session's own work, and every one was real
items.evidence: The worst: the pre-cohort invitation added to /stats embedded the opt-in button, but bindConsent had already run and only on the consent shell — so the primary call to action of the new surface was inert on click, in exactly the state the surface was built for. Two dead-code paths carried comments asserting behaviour the code did not have (observeBackgroundTask resolves rather than rejects, so a trailing .catch was unreachable and 'failures still surface in the panel' was false). The ?dev=1 reveal ran after hydration's failure throw, hiding the diagnostics block — including its retry button — exactly when a degraded domain made it worth reading. task-slice used continue where it meant break. ledger-roll's second --apply would have eaten its own archive header and re-archived its own pointer prose. And the rival-club gate branch had no empty-match guard — a branch whose regex I hand-repaired this session without noticing it could never have warned me. All ten are fixed and pinned by twelve regression tests that fail on the shape that shipped an hour earlier.

items.title: The project's own gates caught three more defects before the review did, and each was obeyed rather than accommodated
items.evidence: check-windows-hide refused a raw node:child_process import in the new sitemap stamper (CANON-016 routes every spawn through the hardened wrapper so a build does not flash a console window per git call). shard-coverage found all four new S94 suites unassigned, so npm test and CI would have skipped them silently while every local run passed — tests that never run are worse than no tests because they read as coverage. And adding document-agreement to the edge attestation correctly turned a green fixture HOLD; the tempting fix was to relax the conjunction, and instead the fixture was corrected and two cases added pinning the states that matter: everything green except a refused document must be HOLD (which is precisely what production was in), and an absent document must read UNPROVED rather than passing by silence.

items.title: The measured-realism story left the debug panels and became the public differentiator it always was
items.evidence: This project holds elite talent to a ceiling sourced from real, structurally stable NFL honor formats — 26 First-Team All-Pro places and 88 Pro Bowl places over the real 1,696-player active population, which is also this game's own ROSTER_STRUCTURE.activeLimit times its team count, so anchor and measured population line up by construction. That story existed in internal notes and in three developer diagnostic panels buried in Settings. New /simulation.html publishes it, spends its longest section on where the analogy breaks down (an award for how someone played is not a claim about how good they are; structural counts are not a measured distribution; a window is part of a measurement; a mean hides a shape), and renders every figure from progressionParity's own constants through comment sentinels — so the page exists in source for the dev server and browser suite, is regenerated by the build, and is asserted in both. A hand-written friendlier number fails the gate.

items.title: Repository and context weight fell by two thirds, with integrity verified before either change was kept
items.evidence: docs/visual-qa held 821 tracked PNGs at 104.9 MB in a public repository whose entire pack was 43.8 MB, growing 84 captures per visual session. The prune was justified by receipts that covered one session, so the 819-entry hash ledger was written first (143 KB, append-only, superseded digests retained) and the prune made to refuse without it: 104.9 MB -> 33.9 MB, every removed capture still provable. It then proved itself in practice — S94's own captures arrived, S89's rolled out, and the archive held at 33.9 MB instead of climbing to 43.8. Separately, five append-only ledgers totalled 861 KB (roughly 215,000 tokens, more than a full context window); rolling entries older than ten sessions verbatim into context/archive took the live set to 439 KB, with every original line confirmed present in either the live file or the archive (136/691/581/1206 lines, 0 missing) before the change was kept. And task-slice.mjs — the bounded read path the audit protocol depends on — did not exist here at all, a silent contract break; it now projects 26 open items into 6 KB from a 158 KB board and says how many it omitted.

followUps.title: Gate the long-horizon facility equilibrium — still evidenced by a probe and asserted by nothing
followUps.evidence: Carried unchanged from S93 and now twice-booked. The season-15 dispersion turnaround (5.658 -> 4.015 -> 3.655 -> 4.050) is the entire justification for adding annual upkeep, and no test asserts the league still has facility spread after a long seeded run. This is the 'argued rather than gated' shape this project keeps re-finding, and S94 deliberately did not rank it because it was already booked.

followUps.title: Verify the beacon actually reports, not merely that the policy admits it
followUps.evidence: The negative control proves the old policy refused both origins and the new one admits them, but admitted is not reporting. Confirm a real pageview lands in the Cloudflare Web Analytics dashboard after the S94 candidate reaches production, and treat a still-silent dashboard as a live finding rather than a deploy delay.

followUps.title: Run /code-review before the canonical receipt, not after
followUps.evidence: This session ran it late. It found ten real defects, which invalidated a completed 45-minute six-shard run that had to be repeated in full. The review costs a fraction of the receipt and belongs in front of it. Booked to the task board as process, not as a task.

followUps.title: Calibrate owner.cash scale and source FACILITY_MARKET_PROFILE's appetite weights
followUps.evidence: Both carried from S93 and both more load-bearing now: owner.cash gates facility construction and upkeep and has made the 35M/80M cashPressure thresholds reachable for the first time, and its magnitude has never been calibrated for a league where cash actually moves. The appetite weights are judgement rather than measurement, making them the newest un-sourced constants in the codebase — the exact shape S92 removed from the elite-density ceiling.

blockers.title: Public launch remains HOLD — launchReady stays false
blockers.evidence: Unchanged and untouched by this session: email-delivery-unverified, founder-approval-unverified, lifecycle-authority-unverified. All three are externally owned and none can be resolved from this repository.

blockers.title: check-release-evidence-freshness is expired, and was before this session
blockers.evidence: Backend release evidence observed 2026-08-16 and expired 2026-08-17 — a week before S94 opened. Tied to the same external launch blockers. Reported rather than masked; not caused by and not addressed by this session.

blockers.title: Registry reports SPARKED against a local FORGE contract
blockers.evidence: Pre-existing authoritative-registry drift, surfaced by lifecycle-coherence as a non-blocking warning. Reconcile through the Studio Ark owner; never edit sibling truth directly.

honestyLedger.title: Two canonical suite runs, the first thrown away — and the reason is a result, not an excuse
honestyLedger.evidence: Run 1 reached the studio shard and failed on three genuine defects in this session's own work: a raw child_process import, four unassigned test suites, and an attestation fixture that correctly turned HOLD. None were flakiness. All three were root-fixed and the run repeated in full rather than reported with a caveat. The receipt of record is run 2: 1,266/1,266, direct exit 0, behavioural source frozen beforehand.

honestyLedger.title: A string replacement deleted code it was not meant to touch, and only a syntax check caught it
honestyLedger.evidence: The first attempt at the app.js review fix over-consumed and removed an unrelated if/else plus a function header. node --check caught it immediately; the file was restored from HEAD and the change re-applied surgically, ending at 24 insertions and 10 deletions with nothing else touched. The quieter version of the same failure had already happened twice this session — two ledger-roll.mjs edits silently no-op'd because the replacement did not match, and a dry run masked it by never reaching the affected code path. The lesson is recorded in the improvement loop: verify the edit landed, do not trust that it did.

honestyLedger.title: Two Playwright failures are pre-existing and are not claimed as green
honestyLedger.evidence: tests-ui/app.spec.js 'season awards and hall of fame history' and 'roster window map' fail on this machine. They were confirmed pre-existing by stashing the entire S94 tree and reproducing both failures against the prior revision. They are disclosed here rather than folded into a pass count.

honestyLedger.title: One ranked item was skipped and three were narrowed, all recorded on the audit item itself
honestyLedger.evidence: The audit JSON carries per-item outcomes including 'skipped-premise-corrected', 'shipped-corrected', 'shipped-reduced' and 'shipped-with-correction', each stating what the original premise claimed and what checking it revealed. The cache-policy item in particular shipped at deliberately reduced scope: a cache-first service worker already precaches 192 assets, so full-graph hashing would have bought far less than the audit assumed and was not pursued for symmetry.

honestyLedger.title: State-vector, entropy and genome refresh scripts do not exist in this repository
honestyLedger.evidence: render-state-vector.mjs, compute-entropy.mjs, append-genome-snapshot.mjs and ignis-rescore-touched.mjs are absent here; the closeout protocol names them as commands. Reported as absent rather than improvised, per the rule that gates are named as commands and failed gates are reported rather than masked.

diffStat.suite: 1,266/1,266 across all six shards (core 194, runtime 740, sim-contract 79, sim-realism 1, long 5, studio 247), direct exit 0 — up from 1,220 (+46 tests, 12 of them regressions pinning defects found in this session's own work), read from the source-bound receipt rather than a wrapper status. Plus 18/18 Playwright specs across the three affected suites. Runtime, sim-contract, sim-realism and long unchanged from S93, the correct signal for a session that moved surfaces and gates without touching simulation behaviour. Doctor blockingFailing 0, 10/12, warnings 2 (both externally owned). Note: the bulk of the file count is 563 deleted visual-QA captures and four archived context ledgers, not code.
